content:
High-frequency eddy current heating typically operates in the range of 10 kHz to several hundred kHz to achieve sufficient penetration and heating effect in metals.  
Option (A) 1 kHz is too low for effective high-frequency heating.  
Option (B) 5 kHz is still relatively low.  
Option (C) 10 MHz is too high for typical industrial eddy current heating and more suited to induction hardening or very shallow heating.  
Option (D) 10 kHz to 400 kHz matches the standard industrial frequency range for eddy current heating applications.  

Final answer: (D)
